messages.content: Three ways to stop a double charge when the worker times out after a 201. Then the one you'd commit.

<think>
[frame: pathway=s2|mode=code|construct=coder|persona=neutral|identity=none|theme=none|channel=reasoning]
A sleep-and-retry hopes the second call is harmless, and it isn't. A flag after the response is missing exactly when the response died. A key written before the call, resent unchanged, is the one the vendor can dedupe. I'd commit the key. The other two are real designs and they fail on this timeout.
</think>

Commit the idempotency key, stored before the call. A retry delay and a flag written after the response both still double-charge when the 201 is the part that got lost.
